ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows triangle KHM, with J on side KH, P on side HM, and L on side MK. Segments KP, HL, and JM are all drawn and intersect at point Q. On segment KP, KQ is labeled as 7, and QP is labeled as 2x - 6. The problem states that J, P, and L are respectively the midpoints of KH, HM, and MK. Reasoning: Because P is the midpoint of HM, KP is the median from vertex K to the midpoint of the opposite side. J and L are also the midpoints of the corresponding sides, so the three segments are the medians of the triangle and intersect at centroid Q. The centroid divides each median in a 2:1 ratio, and the part near the vertex is longer. Therefore on median KP, KQ:QP = 2:1. Given KQ = 7, therefore QP = 7/2 = 3.5. Also in the figure QP = 2x - 6, so 2x - 6 = 3.5, obtaining 2x = 9.5, x = 4.75.

raw_record.question_text: If $J$, $P$, and $L$ are the midpoints of $\overline{KH}$, $\overline{HM}$, and $\overline{MK}$, respectively, find $x$.

method.method_draft: From the image, identify triangle KHM with P on side HM, J on side KH, and L on side MK. The segment KP is drawn as a median and contains point Q, with KQ labeled 7 and QP labeled 2x - 6. From the text, P is the midpoint of HM, and J and L are also midpoints, so the three drawn segments are medians meeting at Q. Use the centroid theorem: the centroid divides each median in a 2:1 ratio, with the longer part adjacent to the vertex. Therefore on median KP, KQ:QP = 2:1. Set 7:(2x - 6) = 2:1, so 2x - 6 = 3.5, giving x = 4.75.
method.CoT_raw:

推理：因为 P 是 HM 的中点，所以 KP 是从顶点 K 到对边中点的中线。J、L 也是对应边的中点，因此三条线段是三角形的中线，并交于重心 Q。重心把每条中线按 2:1 分割，且靠近顶点的部分较长。所以在中线 KP 上，KQ:QP = 2:1。已知 KQ = 7，因此 QP = 7/2 = 3.5。又图中 QP = 2x - 6，所以 2x - 6 = 3.5，得到 2x = 9.5，x = 4.75。

method.method_draft: Use an affine/coordinate derivation instead of quoting the centroid ratio directly. From the image, focus on median KP: KQ is labeled 7 and QP is labeled 2x - 6. From the text, P is the midpoint of HM, while J and L are midpoints of the other sides, so Q is the intersection of medians. Assign convenient coordinates to the triangle, for example let K, H, and M have position vectors k, h, and m. Since P is the midpoint of HM, p = (h + m)/2. The median intersection/centroid has position q = (k + h + m)/3. Along median KP, q = k + (2/3)(p - k), so KQ is 2/3 of KP and QP is 1/3 of KP. Thus KQ = 2(QP). Using the image labels, 7 = 2(2x - 6), so 2x - 6 = 3.5 and x = 4.75.
